baseline.clone_argfilter: For both clone and clone3, filter on the flags argument with SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ to require all CLONE_NEW* bits to be CLEAR, allowing thread creation but blocking new namespaces. Mask = CLONE_NEWNS|CLONE_NEWCGROUP|CLONE_NEWUTS|CLONE_NEWIPC|CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWPID|CLONE_NEWNET|CLONE_NEWTIME = 0x7e020080; rule = ALLOW only when (flags & 0x7e020080) == 0, else ERRNO(EPERM). Individual bit values (uapi/linux/sched.h): CLONE_NEWTIME=0x00000080, CLONE_NEWNS=0x00020000, CLONE_NEWCGROUP=0x02000000, CLONE_NEWUTS=0x04000000, CLONE_NEWIPC=0x08000000, CLONE_NEWUSER=0x10000000, CLONE_NEWPID=0x20000000, CLONE_NEWNET=0x40000000. Caveat for clone (legacy): flags is arg0 and its low byte is CSIGNAL (exit_signal) which overlaps nothing in the mask, so masking is safe; CLONE_NEWTIME(0x80) sits in CSIGNAL range only for the legacy clone exit-signal byte (0xff) -- in practice thread creation uses exit_signal=0 so masking 0x80 is still correct, but if a libc ever passed exit_signal bits that collide, prefer the clone3 path. For clone3 the flags live in struct clone_args in memory and are NOT directly reachable by classic seccomp (seccomp only sees the pointer in arg0), so clone3 CANNOT be flag-filtered by cBPF -- the safe policy is: allow clone (flag-masked as above) and DENY clone3 with ENOSYS so libcs fall back to clone. glibc>=2.34 and musl both fall back to clone when clone3 returns ENOSYS. Observed thread-create flags in all of glibc/musl/go: CLONE_VM|CLONE_FS|CLONE_FILES|CLONE_SIGHAND|CLONE_THREAD|CLONE_SYSVSEM|CLONE_SETTLS(|CLONE_PARENT_SETTID|CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID) -- none set any CLONE_NEW* bit.
baseline.method: Empirical strace on x86_64 (Linux 7.0, kernel uapi at /usr/src/linux.git). Built 5 native binaries from a thread+file+poll+sleep workload (work.c: 4 pthreads doing compute, open/read/write/lseek/fstat/stat, readlink /proc/self/exe, opendir/readdir/getdents, /dev/null poll + epoll_create1/ctl/wait, clock_gettime, nanosleep, getpid/uid/gid; work.go: 4 goroutines + os file IO + ReadDir + sleep): (1) glibc dynamic PIE (system gcc -pthread), (2) glibc static (gcc -static -pthread), (3) musl dynamic and (4) musl static via the OpenWrt x86_64 musl toolchain at /usr/src/openwrt/staging_dir/toolchain-x86_64_gcc-14.3.0_musl, (5) Go static (host go1.26). Also straced busybox (OpenWrt build_dir/target-x86_64_musl busybox-1.37.0) running `sh -c :`. Ran `strace -f -qq` on each (musl-dyn and busybox launched via the toolchain libc.so loader with --library-path to the matching musl lib dir), extracted unique syscall names per trace, took the UNION, then removed the excluded categories (execve/execveat, raw socket(), ptrace, mount/umount, and app-specific). clone/clone3 flag values cross-checked against /usr/src/linux.git/include/uapi/linux/sched.h.")
baseline.notes: Empirically observed UNION across the 6 traces (execve dropped per exclusion -- it is only strace's own launch and exec is not part of the container floor): arch_prctl, brk, mmap, mprotect, munmap, madvise, membarrier, rseq, set_tid_address, set_robust_list, futex, getrandom, prlimit64, rt_sigaction, rt_sigprocmask, sigaltstack, clone, clone3, openat, open, close, read, write, writev, pread64, lseek, fstat, newfstatat, stat, getdents64, readlink, readlinkat, fcntl, access, poll, epoll_create1, epoll_ctl, epoll_wait, epoll_pwait, eventfd2, clock_nanosleep, nanosleep, getpid, getppid, gettid, getuid, getgid, prctl, uname, sched_getaffinity/sched_yield (Go scheduler), fsync (Go), exit, exit_group. Per-libc differences: glibc uses clone3+rseq+getrandom+set_robust_list and the *at stat variants (newfstatat); this musl (1.2.6) uses legacy clone + legacy open/stat (no rseq, no getrandom -- it reads /dev/urandom via open instead) + writev; Go uses clone (not clone3), eventfd2, sigaltstack, sched_getaffinity, fsync, gettid, prctl, no rseq. The returned baseline DELIBERATELY SUPERSETS the observed union for cross-arch/cross-version safety (a missing baseline syscall means nothing starts): I added (a) clock_gettime/clock_gettime64/gettimeofday/clock_getres -- routed through the vDSO here so they never appeared in strace, but under a container with no usable vDSO clocksource the vDSO falls back to the real syscall, so they are mandatory; (b) statx -- newer glibc (>=2.33) implements stat()/fstat() via statx, this build still used newfstatat; (c) rt_sigreturn -- never strace-visible unless a signal is actually delivered, but ANY signal-handler return needs it (Go installs sigaltstack handlers); (d) mmap2/fstatat64/fstat64/lstat/getrlimit/set_thread_area -- the 32-bit/other-arch equivalents (set_thread_area is the i386/x86-and-arm TLS setup analogous to arch_prctl(ARCH_SET_FS) on x86_64; arm64/riscv set TLS in clone via CLONE_SETTLS so need no extra call); (e) ppoll/pselect6/select/epoll_create/epoll_pwait2/faccessat2/pipe2/dup/dup3/ioctl/getcwd/sysinfo/getcpu/tgkill/tkill/kill/restart_syscall/futex_waitv/get_robust_list/rt_sigpending/rt_sigtimedwait/getgroups/geteuid/getegid/getpgrp/getpgid/getsid/fdatasync -- standard libc-internal and thread/abort/poll fallbacks present in real ELF runtimes (musl raise()/abort use tgkill; pthread_cancel uses tkill; glibc malloc/getentropy paths). EXCLUDED as requested and NOT in baseline: execve/execveat (no exec floor), socket/socketpair/connect/bind/etc raw socket creation, ptrace/process_vm_*, mount/umount2/pivot_root/chroot, and app-specific (epoll on real fds for servers, inotify, signalfd, timerfd, etc -- add per-app). clone3 should be DENIED with ENOSYS (not flag-filtered) because classic seccomp cannot read struct clone_args through the pointer; libc falls back to flag-masked clone. This list is the floor only -- a network-capable container additionally needs the socket family, which is outside this baseline by the task's own exclusion.

classification.exec_rescore: execve/execveat are reclassified from the prior ALLOW to OPTIN. See notable[]/summary for full reasoning.

notable.name: execve
notable.why: Prior: ALLOW (common, suid-neutralized). Now OPTIN -- exec is the RCE-to-shell pivot; single-binary services never re-exec after the runtime's initial entrypoint exec. Commonality rejected as a justification.

notable.name: execveat
notable.why: Same as execve; fd-based exec is the same pivot, demoted from ALLOW to OPTIN.

notable.name: socket
notable.why: Prior: ALLOW (common). Now OPTIN -- a service that does no networking needs no socket; AF_* reachability and the whole connect/bind/listen surface should be opted into per-package, not granted by default.

notable.name: connect
notable.why: Prior baseline-adjacent ALLOW. Now OPTIN -- outbound connection capability is exactly the kind of network primitive a minimal floor withholds from a non-networked service.

notable.name: bind
notable.why: Listening sockets are a per-package need, not a run-anything baseline; OPTIN.

notable.name: listen
notable.why: Server socket setup; only network services need it; OPTIN.

notable.name: accept4
notable.why: Accepting connections is a network-service capability, withheld on the floor; OPTIN.

notable.name: sendmsg
notable.why: Prior: ALLOW (SCM_RIGHTS netns-confined). Now OPTIN with the socket family -- fd-passing and datagram send are not needed to merely run.

notable.name: setsockopt
notable.why: Prior ALLOW. Now OPTIN -- only meaningful once a socket exists, moves with the network family off the floor.

notable.name: splice
notable.why: Prior: ALLOW (common, Dirty-Pipe was write-side). Now OPTIN -- zero-copy plumbing is a performance feature, not a run requirement; keeps the page-cache-injection class off the default floor.

notable.name: memfd_create
notable.why: Prior: ALLOW (fileless-exec just a building block). Now OPTIN -- anonymous executable-backing memory is the classic pairing for exec-less code loading; withhold by default, re-grant for runtimes that need it.

notable.name: mknod
notable.why: Prior: ALLOW (CAP_MKNOD absent -> FIFO/socket only). Now OPTIN -- device/FIFO node creation is an installer-class need, not a run requirement.

notable.name: mknodat
notable.why: Same CAP_MKNOD framing; demoted to OPTIN with mknod.

notable.name: setxattr
notable.why: Prior implicitly allowed. Now OPTIN -- xattr WRITES (set/remove, l/f and *at variants) can set security.* and trusted.* labels; not needed to merely run, so withheld; reads stay equally non-baseline OPTIN for minimalism.

notable.name: ptrace
notable.why: Unchanged deny but re-tiered HARDDENY: intra-container hijack and seccomp-bypass-of-peer primitive; opt-in discouraged (debug-only containers).

notable.name: clone3
notable.why: Prior: ALLOW (modern runtimes need it). Now HARDDENY -- its CLONE_NEW* flags live in struct clone_args and are UNFILTERABLE by cBPF; deny with ENOSYS so glibc>=2.34/musl fall back to the flag-masked clone. This is the only way to actually block payload re-namespacing, closing the unshare/setns gap the prior analysis left open.

notable.name: clone
notable.why: Stays baseline but now ARG-FILTERED: ALLOW only when (flags & 0x7e020080)==0, else EPERM. Permits thread/process creation while blocking every CLONE_NEW* namespace bit at the register-visible level.

notable.name: name_to_handle_at
notable.why: Prior: DENY (Shocker forging half). Re-tiered OPTIN, not harddeny -- harmless alone (open_by_handle_at stays harddeny), and systemd/util-linux use it for mount-id lookup; re-grantable for init-style payloads.

notable.name: process_vm_readv
notable.why: Prior: DENY. Re-tiered OPTIN -- cross-process READ is an intra-container info-leak, not a host-boundary break; re-grantable for sanitizer/profiler containers. Its write twin stays harddeny.

notable.name: process_vm_writev
notable.why: Cross-process memory WRITE -> intra-container code hijack; opt-in discouraged, HARDDENY.

notable.name: clock_adjtime
notable.why: Prior: DENY. Re-tiered OPTIN -- the slew/step write needs absent CAP_SYS_TIME, but the modes=0 READ path is used by NTP/chrony clients; re-grantable for time-sync payloads. clock_settime/settimeofday stay harddeny (host-global write only).

notable.name: io_setup
notable.why: Prior: ALLOW (libaio compat, broadly allowed). Now OPTIN -- legacy AIO is a DB/storage dependency, not a run requirement; the whole io_* legacy family moves off the floor, still kept distinct from the harddenied io_uring family.

notable.name: io_uring_setup
notable.why: Stays deny, re-tiered HARDDENY -- top recent LPE source; async openat/splice ring is an escape-grade primitive, opt-in discouraged.

notable.name: sched_setscheduler
notable.why: Prior: ALLOW. Now OPTIN -- RT/FIFO scheduling and DEADLINE-DoS knobs are not needed to merely run; sched_getaffinity/yield stay baseline, the setters move to opt-in.

notable.name: seccomp
notable.why: Prior: ALLOW (self-confining). Now OPTIN -- nested self-sandboxing is useful to some apps but not required to run; withheld by default, freely re-grantable since it cannot escape under NNP.

notable.name: mount
notable.why: Mount-table/fs-parser surface; the whole mount + new-mount-API family (fsopen/fsconfig/fsmount/fspick/move_mount/open_tree*/mount_setattr) is HARDDENY, re-grant discouraged.

notable.name: syslog
notable.why: Prior: ALLOW (borderline keep). Now OPTIN -- kernel ring-buffer access is not a run requirement and risks dmesg leakage; re-grantable for log tools.

classification.summary: The floor shrinks from an allowlist of roughly 300+ effective names (the moby/containers-common lineage minus ~26 real drops -- still permitting exec, the full socket/network family, all xattrs, splice, memfd_create, mknod, legacy AIO, the scheduler setters, seccomp, etc.) down to a hard-coded irreducible BASELINE of 96 syscalls (95 unconditional + clone arg-filtered). That is roughly a 3x reduction in default-reachable surface. The governing rule is inverted: the prior analysis kept a syscall if it was common OR allowed by the surveyed runtimes; this floor explicitly REJECTS commonality and runtime-consensus as justifications and admits a syscall to baseline ONLY if it is needed to merely run a single-binary service after the runtime has exec'd the entrypoint. Everything else is DENY-by-default and re-grantable per-package via CONTAINER_SECCOMP_ALLOW (optin), except true escape/host-compromise primitives which are harddeny (deny, opt-in discouraged). Key movements OFF the baseline into OPTIN: the entire exec family (the RCE-to-shell pivot -- the headline correction), the entire network family (socket/socketcall/connect/bind/listen/accept*/send*/recv*/setsockopt/getsockopt -- a non-networked service needs none), all xattr writes AND reads, filesystem mutation (mkdir/unlink/rename/link/symlink/chmod/chown/truncate/fallocate and *at variants), splice/tee/copy_file_range/sendfile, memfd_create, mknod*, the timer/inotify/signalfd/eventfd auxiliary fd families, the SysV+POSIX IPC families, legacy AIO (io_setup/io_submit/...), the scheduler/priority setters, the credential setters beyond identity reads, seccomp, landlock, openat2/creat, name_to_handle_at, process_vm_readv, and clock_adjtime/adjtimex (read path). Two classifications change tier vs the prior pass on security grounds: clone3 moves to HARDDENY (its struct-hidden CLONE_NEW* flags cannot be cBPF-filtered, so it is denied with ENOSYS to force the glibc/musl fallback onto the flag-masked clone, which alone makes the no-re-namespacing guarantee real), while clone stays baseline but is arg-filtered (ALLOW iff (flags & 0x7e020080)==0). The harddeny tier keeps the full module/mount/new-mount-API/kexec/keyring/bpf/perf/io_uring/time-set/raw-IO/hardware-MMIO(incl. s390_pci_mmio_*)/unshare/setns/open_by_handle_at/ptrace/process_vm_writev/userfaultfd/modify_ldt families plus the dead/obsolete pseudo-syscalls. Net: a genuinely minimal, force-explicit baseline where running a service grants nothing beyond CPU, memory, existing-fd I/O, time reads, identity reads, threading (no namespaces), and signals -- and every capability a real app wants (network, exec, filesystem writes, IPC, xattrs) is an explicit, auditable per-package opt-in.

construction.construction:
INVERT THE MODEL: switch from "moby ALLOW base MINUS tighten.list" (deny-delta) to "explicit baseline ALLOW set PLUS per-package additions, defaultAction ERRNO" (allow-floor). Concretely, the render becomes a set algebra over name-sets plus a small static table of arg-filtered rules:

floor_allow(arch, pkg) =
  ( baseline_allow                      # the hardcoded ~150-name list from the task
    UNION words(CONTAINER_SECCOMP_ALLOW) # per-package opt-ins
  )
  INTERSECT arch_available(arch)        # drop names this arch never has
  MINUS arg_filtered_names              # names that are handled by an arg-filter rule instead of a plain ALLOW

Output JSON:
  defaultAction: SCMP_ACT_ERRNO
  defaultErrnoRet: 38 (ENOSYS, copied from base) -- everything not in the floor returns ENOSYS so libcs feature-probe-fallback cleanly; the few rules that need EPERM/EINVAL carry their own errnoRet.
  architectures: [scmp_arch (+ subarch)] from platmap
  syscalls:
    (1) one group: { names: <plain floor names, sorted>, action: SCMP_ACT_ALLOW }
    (2) the arg-filter rules, emitted verbatim, ONLY for names that are in the resolved floor:
        - clone   : ALLOW when (flags & 0x7e020080)==0 via SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ, else fall through to defaultAction (ERRNO/ENOSYS). Always emitted (clone is in baseline_allow).
        - clone3  : NOT in baseline_allow and NOT addable -> never emitted as ALLOW, so it hits defaultAction. To force ENOSYS specifically (not whatever default is) we may emit an explicit { names:["clone3"], action: SCMP_ACT_ERRNO, errnoRet: 38 } so the deny is pinned to ENOSYS regardless of any future default change -- this is what makes glibc>=2.34/musl fall back to clone.
        - socket / personality / etc.: pulled from seccomp-base.json's arg-filter rules, but ONLY copied through when the bare syscall name is present in the resolved floor (e.g. socket only appears if a package opts it in via CONTAINER_SECCOMP_ALLOW). When copied, the base's caps-conditional excludes are dropped (floor has zero caps, so the "no CAP_AUDIT_WRITE" branch is the only reachable one -- we keep exactly that branch).

arch_available(arch): there is NO standalone per-arch syscall table in the tree, and we don't want to add a 7-arch kernel-uapi table to maintain. Use the moby base as the arch oracle: a name is "available on arch" if some group in seccomp-base.json lists that name AND that group's includes.arches is empty (all-arch) OR contains p.arch. Names in baseline_allow that the base never mentions are kept unconditionally (they are core and the base is just incomplete for newer calls like futex_waitv/epoll_pwait2/clock_*_time64 -- those are guarded by being no-ops on arches lacking them). This keeps the existing arch_token_allowed() logic, just repurposed from "which base groups survive" to "is this floor name plausible on this arch".

Net effect vs today: exec*, mount*, ptrace, bpf, the whole socket family, fork/vfork, setuid family, *xattr, etc. are NOT in baseline_allow, so they are denied by omission rather than by an ever-growing tighten.list. The deny-delta file disappears; the floor is positive and auditable as a single list.
files: /usr/src/openwrt-stuff/containers/files/seccomp-baseline.list (NEW: the explicit baseline_allow set, one syscall per line + justification; replaces seccomp-tighten.list as the editable policy surface)
/usr/src/openwrt-stuff/containers/files/seccomp-tighten.list (DELETE / archive: deny-delta no longer used by the renderer; keep under reviews/ for provenance only)

/usr/src/openwrt-stuff/containers/files/seccomp-base.json (KEEP, role narrowed: now only the source of (a) arch metadata via archMap/includes.arches and (b) the arg-filter rule bodies for clone/socket/personality; its plain ALLOW groups are no longer the floor)

/usr/src/openwrt-stuff/containers/container.mk (CHANGED: wire seccomp-render into Build/Compile, pass CONTAINER_SECCOMP_ALLOW + platform, and have oci-policy.uc OR a follow-on step splice the rendered profile into config.json)
/usr/src/openwrt-stuff/containers/files/oci-policy.uc (CHANGED: set cfg.linux.seccomp from the rendered profile -- today it sets caps/ns/limits/devices but never touches seccomp at all)
/usr/src/openwrt-stuff/containers/files/seccomp-profile.uc (NEW, optional tracing helper: ingest strace/auditd/SCMP_ACT_LOG output, emit a CONTAINER_SECCOMP_ALLOW line)
construction.render_changes:
seccomp-render.uc rewrite (signature: seccomp-render.uc <baseline.list> <base.json> <platform> <seccomp_allow_string> <out.json>):

1. Keep platmap + arch resolution exactly as today (lines 21-41).
2. Parse baseline.list the same way tighten.list is parsed today (trim, skip blank/#, take first token), but push into a baseline_allow set (a {} used as a string-set) instead of drop_names. The big inline list in the task literally becomes the seed of this file.
3. Parse the seccomp_allow argv string with the same words()/split(/[ \t]+/) helper oci-policy.uc uses; UNION each token into baseline_allow. (Tokens may be bare names; a future @cap-group expansion can map a group name to base names, mirroring tighten.list's '@' convention -- but for the floor, prefer explicit names.)
4. Build arch_available from base.json: iterate base.syscalls, and for every name in a group whose includes has empty/absent .arches OR .arches contains p.arch, mark arch_seen[name]=true. Also record which names appear in any caps-gated group (so we never silently re-add a cap-only call: if a baseline name only ever appears caps-gated in base, that's fine -- baseline is authoritative, base is only the arch oracle).
5. arg_filtered = { clone:true, clone3:true, socket:true, personality:true } -- the set of names whose behaviour is a rule, not a plain ALLOW. Build it dynamically by scanning base.syscalls for any group with length(args)>0 and remembering those names.
6. Compose plain_names = sort( name in baseline_allow where (arch_seen[name] OR not base_mentions[name]) AND not arg_filtered[name] ). Emit one { names: plain_names, action: SCMP_ACT_ALLOW } group.
7. clone rule: always emit (clone is core). Hardcode the masked-eq rule (see clone_argfilter_spec). Do NOT pull clone's rule from base -- base allows clone unconditionally; we are tightening it.
8. clone3 rule: emit { names:["clone3"], action: SCMP_ACT_ERRNO, errnoRet: 38 } unconditionally (pin ENOSYS for libc fallback). Never list clone3 in plain_names.
9. For each OTHER arg_filtered name (socket, personality), only if it is in the resolved baseline_allow (i.e. opted in): copy the matching ALLOW rule-bodies out of base.syscalls, taking only the branches whose excludes.caps is non-empty/cap-gated-away-from-us (floor has zero caps, so the cap-excluded ALLOW branch is the live one) and dropping includes/excludes/comment, keeping names/action/args/errnoRet. For socket specifically this reproduces the moby AF_NETLINK(=16) handling exactly as the task requires.
10. Output object identical shape to today (defaultAction/architectures/syscalls/defaultErrnoRet), written with sprintf("%.J\n", out).

Caller/wiring change: container.mk Build/Compile gains, before oci-policy.uc runs:
  $(UCODE) $(CONTAINER_SECCOMP_RENDER) $(SECCOMP_BASELINE_LIST) $(SECCOMP_BASE_JSON) $(CONTAINER_OCI_PLATFORM) "$(CONTAINER_SECCOMP_ALLOW)" $(PKG_BUILD_DIR)/seccomp.json
and policy.kv gains seccomp_profile=$(PKG_BUILD_DIR)/seccomp.json. oci-policy.uc reads pol.seccomp_profile and does cfg.linux.seccomp = read_json(pol.seccomp_profile) (new ~3 lines near the device block at line 173). All vars declared at top of their function per OpenWrt C89-style ucode convention the user enforces.
construction.clone_argfilter_spec:
clone (only; clone3 is denied, not filtered):

Mask of all CLONE_NEW* bits to forbid:
  CLONE_NEWTIME   0x00000080
  CLONE_NEWNS     0x00020000
  CLONE_NEWCGROUP 0x02000000
  CLONE_NEWUTS    0x04000000
  CLONE_NEWIPC    0x08000000
  CLONE_NEWUSER   0x10000000
  CLONE_NEWPID    0x20000000
  CLONE_NEWNET    0x40000000
  MASK = 0x7e020080

Rule (libseccomp/OCI semantics -- a syscall rule matches only when ALL its args[] predicates are true; non-matching falls through to defaultAction):
  {
    "names": ["clone"],
    "action": "SCMP_ACT_ALLOW",
    "args": [
      { "index": 0, "value": 2113937536, "valueTwo": 0, "op": "SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ" }
    ]
  }
  where 2113937536 == 0x7e020080 (the mask) and valueTwo (the required result) == 0.
  SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ semantics: (arg0 & value) == valueTwo, i.e. (flags & 0x7e020080) == 0 -> ALLOW; any CLONE_NEW* bit set -> NOT matched -> defaultAction == SCMP_ACT_ERRNO. To make that denial EPERM rather than the default ENOSYS, also emit a SECOND lower-priority deny rule is NOT possible in flat OCI (no rule ordering guarantee for same syscall with overlapping masks), so accept defaultErrnoRet(ENOSYS) for the blocked-namespace case; ENOSYS on clone-with-NEWNS is harmless (no libc thread path sets those bits). The task asked for EPERM; note that flat seccomp profiles cannot express "match-and-EPERM" as a fall-through, only "match-and-ALLOW". If EPERM is mandatory, invert: defaultErrnoRet stays ENOSYS globally but we cannot per-syscall override the no-match path -- so document EPERM-on-NEWNS as a non-goal of the cBPF floor and rely on the user-namespace + dropped CAP_SYS_ADMIN making the unshare/clone-NEWNS attempt fail at the kernel boundary anyway.

index 0 is correct for both glibc (clone(flags,...)) and the raw syscall on all our target arches EXCEPT that the legacy clone ABI argument ORDER differs on some arches; libseccomp normalises arg indices to the C-library prototype order, and the OCI runtime (ujail/runc-style) feeds libseccomp, so index:0 == flags is the libseccomp-normalised view -> portable across amd64/arm64/arm/x86/riscv64. CSIGNAL low-byte caveat: exit_signal occupies bits 0..7 (0xff); our mask's only overlap there is CLONE_NEWTIME(0x80). Real thread creation passes exit_signal==0, so (flags & 0x80)==0 holds and threads are allowed; a hypothetical libc passing exit_signal with bit7 set would be mis-blocked, which is exactly why clone3 is denied-with-ENOSYS to force the well-behaved clone path rather than relying on clone3's in-memory flags that cBPF cannot read.

clone3: cannot be flag-filtered (flags live in struct clone_args behind the arg0 pointer; cBPF sees only the pointer). Policy: { "names":["clone3"], "action":"SCMP_ACT_ERRNO", "errnoRet": 38 } (ENOSYS) so glibc>=2.34 and musl fall back to clone, which IS filtered.
construction.profile_tooling:
FEASIBLE, and largely already prototyped: seccomp-analysis.json (385 syscalls, 12 runtimes, per-call danger score + decision + rationale) shows this corpus-driven approach is already in use; the per-package helper is the same idea narrowed to one image.

Recommended discovery path, in order of fidelity:

1. SCMP_ACT_LOG dry-run (best). Render a "learning" profile identical to the floor but with defaultAction=SCMP_ACT_LOG instead of ERRNO (one-line render flag). Run the container on the VM with this profile, exercise it (start + healthcheck + its real workload). The kernel logs every syscall that WOULD have been denied to the audit/dmesg ring as "seccomp ... syscall=<nr>". Collect with `dmesg`/`ausearch -m SECCOMP`, map nr->name per arch (need an arch syscall-number table -- the one place a small per-arch nr<->name map is genuinely required; ausearch already prints names on most setups via /usr/include or audit's own table). Union the captured names into the existing floor and emit a CONTAINER_SECCOMP_ALLOW=... line. This is non-fatal (LOG doesn't break the app) so you get a COMPLETE used-set in one run, not a fail-iterate loop.

2. strace fallback (no kernel audit). `strace -ff -qq -e trace=all -o trace container...`, then `grep -hoE '^[a-z_0-9]+\(' trace.* | tr -d '(' | sort -u`. Simpler, arch-name-native (strace prints names), but perturbs timing and needs ptrace available in the harness (build host or VM, NOT inside the floored container). Good enough for build-time profiling on the host before sealing.

3. Static seed from seccomp-analysis.json: pre-populate a candidate allow set from the runtimes_allowing>=N consensus to shrink the iterate count, then confirm with (1).

Where to run: build-time on the host is cheapest but only sees the build/start path; the on-VM SCMP_ACT_LOG run is authoritative because it sees the real workload (and the user's MEMORY notes the VM reboot/deploy flow already). Propose a make target `container-profile` that does the LOG render + emits a suggested CONTAINER_SECCOMP_ALLOW for the maintainer to paste into the package Makefile (NOT auto-applied -- the allow-list is policy and must be reviewed, mirroring how seccomp-tighten.list carries per-line justification today).

Cost/honesty: yes, with exec/socket/fork denied by default EVERY package needs a profile -- there is no universal floor that runs an arbitrary image. That is the intended tradeoff: a shell-less single-binary Go service (traefik-whoami, already validated e2e per MEMORY) needs ~baseline only; anything that fork/execs a helper, opens AF_INET sockets, or spawns a supervisor needs an explicit, reviewed addition. The tooling makes the addition discoverable in one LOG run rather than guesswork; that is what keeps the strict floor maintainable across a fleet.

verdicts.lens: FALSE-DENY (executed test binaries under the candidate filter for real)
verdicts.evidence:
Built and ran four real targets on x86_64 (kernel 7.0.10), each under a raw-BPF seccomp(2)+prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS) harness that ALLOWs ONLY the baseline_allow syscall numbers with defaultAction=SCMP_ACT_ERRNO/ENOSYS(38) and an arch-guard. Targets: (a) static-musl C via OpenWrt x86_64-musl-gcc 14.3.0 `-static` (/tmp/sccfloor/hello_static_musl), (b) dynamic-glibc C via gcc 16.1.1 PIE (/tmp/sccfloor/hello_dyn_glibc), (c) Go 1.26 CGO_ENABLED=0 (/tmp/sccfloor/hello_go), (d) OpenWrt x86_64-musl busybox 1.37.0 `sh -c :` run via its ld-musl loader with LD_LIBRARY_PATH to the musl rootfs.

baseline_allow resolved to 91 numbered syscalls on x86_64; 4 names are 32-bit-only and absent here (fstatat64, mmap2, clock_gettime64, clock_nanosleep_time64) -- expected.

STRICT LITERAL FLOOR (exactly baseline_allow, nothing added): ALL FOUR targets fail to even launch -- the harness's execvp returns errno=38 ENOSYS. execve(59)/execveat(322) are NOT in baseline_allow, so under a literal floor an OCI runtime cannot exec the entrypoint and NO container can start. This is a universal FALSE-DENY for container start.

FLOOR + execve/execveat ONLY: all four run to completion, exit 0 (static-musl prints hello-from-c; glibc prints hello-from-c; Go prints hello-from-go sum=499500; busybox sh -c : exits 0; busybox sh -c 'echo hi' prints hi). strace cross-check: the ONLY syscall outside the floor that any of the four single-binary targets issues is execve itself (glibc dynamic loader, musl, and the Go runtime are all fully satisfied by the floor: clone for threads, futex, madvise, mmap, mprotect, arch_prctl, rt_sig*, sched_getaffinity, sigaltstack, set_tid_address, set_robust_list, rseq, getrandom, gettid, openat, read, close, fcntl, prctl).

REAL arg-filtered-clone floor (built harness_real.c implementing clone ALLOW iff (flags & 0x7e020080)==0, plus execve/execveat, defaultAction ENOSYS): all four still run to completion. Go thread-creation clone flags = 0x003d0f00, (flags & 0x7e020080)==0 -> permitted. Negative control: raw clone(CLONE_NEWNS|SIGCHLD) is denied with errno=38 ENOSYS, confirming the no-re-namespacing guarantee. The mask blocks exactly the 7 CLONE_NEW* namespace bits.

clone3: none of the four runtimes call it (0 calls each via strace); glibc 2.43/musl/Go all use clone here. So HARDDENY-clone3 is harmless in practice -- the fallback path works.

SHELL-PIPELINE probe (beyond a single-binary service): busybox `sh -c '( true ) | ( true )'` fails under the floor -- it needs pipe(22) [floor has only pipe2], dup2(33) [floor has only dup/dup3], fork(57) [floor has only clone], and wait4(61) [absent]. Observed error 'sh: can't create pipe: Bad file descriptor' then ENOSYS on fork/wait4. A single busybox `sh -c 'extcmd'` does NOT fork (tail-call execve optimization) so it passes; only real forking/pipeline orchestration hits these.
issues: CRITICAL/by-design-but-must-be-flagged: execve and execveat are NOT in baseline_allow. Under the literal floor, executed for real, every one of the four binaries fails to launch with ENOSYS -- no container can start. The OCI runtime execs the entrypoint with the filter already installed, so execve(59)+execveat(322) are an irreducible required addition for ANY container. The classification frames exec as 'OPTIN per-package', but that makes exec a mandatory opt-in for 100% of packages, i.e. it is effectively part of the floor for the entrypoint launch. The floor JSON as specified (execve omitted, defaultErrnoRet=38) cannot start a service.

Legacy fork(57) is omitted (floor has clone only). Verified: the musl busybox uses raw fork() for pipelines and gets ENOSYS. Any glibc/musl/app that calls fork() directly rather than via the clone wrapper, or on builds where the libc fork path uses SYS_fork, will FALSE-DENY. The four hello-world targets happen to use clone, but fork is a common single-process primitive (e.g. daemon double-fork, popen, system()).

pipe(22) omitted (floor has pipe2 only): verified ENOSYS in busybox pipeline ('can't create pipe: Bad file descriptor'). Any binary using the legacy pipe() syscall (older glibc paths, some statically-linked tooling) FALSE-DENYs.

dup2(33) omitted (floor has dup/dup3 only): verified used by busybox for fd redirection. dup2 is extremely common for stdio redirection (daemons reopening 0/1/2 to /dev/null, log fds). A real single-binary service that redirects its own stdio via dup2 will FALSE-DENY. dup3 requires flags and many libcs still emit dup2.
wait4(61)/waitid(247) omitted entirely: any service that reaps a child (popen/system/posix_spawn-then-wait, or a supervisor entrypoint) FALSE-DENYs. Verified ENOSYS in the busybox pipeline.

INCONSISTENCY in the spec vs classification: the literal baseline_allow array CONTAINS 'clone3', but the classification text says clone3 must be HARDDENY (emit explicit ENOSYS) to force the clone fallback. If the render literally ALLOWs the baseline_allow names, clone3 would be allowed -- contradicting the stated security goal. The render must special-case clone3 OUT of the plain-allow group; tested-harmless because no runtime here uses clone3, but the spec is self-contradictory.

posix_spawn note: glibc/musl posix_spawn uses clone(CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK) or clone3; with the arg-filter mask 0x7e020080, CLONE_VFORK(0x4000) is NOT masked so clone-based posix_spawn would pass the flag filter, but it still needs execve (added) and wait* (NOT in floor) to be useful -- another reason exec-capable services also need wait4.

verdicts.lens: FALSE-ALLOW: verify the strict seccomp baseline contains no exploit-pivot syscalls (exec, socket/socketcall, ptrace, clone3, mount*, open_by_handle_at, bpf, keyring/module families) and that clone is arg-filtered not name-allowed.
verdicts.evidence: Programmatically intersected the given baseline_allow (95 unique names, no duplicates) against every forbidden exploit-pivot family. Clean results for nearly all: NONE of execve/execveat, socket/socketcall/connect/bind/listen/accept*/send*/recv*/setsockopt/getsockopt/socketpair, ptrace/process_vm_readv/process_vm_writev, mount/umount*/move_mount/open_tree/fsopen/fsconfig/fsmount/fspick/pivot_root/chroot, name_to_handle_at/open_by_handle_at, bpf, add_key/request_key/keyctl, init_module/finit_module/delete_module, unshare/setns, perf_event_open/kexec*/userfaultfd/modify_ldt/io_uring* appear in baseline_allow. The clone arg-filter mask 0x7e020080 is correct: it covers all seven CLONE_NEW* flags (CLONE_NEWNS 0x20000, NEWCGROUP 0x2000000, NEWUTS 0x4000000, NEWIPC 0x8000000, NEWUSER 0x10000000, NEWPID 0x20000000, NEWNET 0x40000000 = 0x7e020000) plus CLONE_VM 0x80, so the ALLOW-iff-(flags&mask)==0 rule genuinely blocks re-namespacing via clone. HOWEVER there is one decisive leak: clone3 IS present in baseline_allow (literally in the list). clone3 has NO arg-filter rule (the static arg-filter table covers only clone/socket/personality), so under the documented render -- group (1) emits all plain floor names as SCMP_ACT_ALLOW -- clone3 would be emitted as an unconditional plain ALLOW.
issues: FALSE-ALLOW (critical): clone3 is in baseline_allow. This directly contradicts the construction spec, which states clone3 must be HARDDENY, NOT in baseline_allow, never emitted as ALLOW, and explicitly pinned to SCMP_ACT_ERRNO/ENOSYS(38). With clone3 in the plain baseline names and no arg-filter rule covering it, the render's group (1) {names:[...], action:SCMP_ACT_ALLOW} would grant clone3 unconditionally.

Security consequence: clone3 passes its flags inside a struct (struct clone_args) in memory, which cBPF/seccomp cannot inspect. An allowed clone3 lets a compromised service set CLONE_NEWUSER/CLONE_NEWNS/CLONE_NEWNET/etc., re-creating namespaces and fully defeating the 'no re-namespacing' guarantee that the arg-filtered clone mask (0x7e020080) exists to enforce. The clone mask is rendered moot -- attacker just calls clone3 instead.

Fallback breakage: the whole point of denying clone3 with ENOSYS is to force glibc>=2.34/musl to fall back onto the flag-masked clone. Allowing clone3 means the libc never falls back, so the masked-clone path is never exercised and the namespace block never applies.

Remediation: remove clone3 from baseline_allow and emit the explicit pinned deny {names:["clone3"], action:SCMP_ACT_ERRNO, errnoRet:38} as the spec's Construction section (2) describes. Verify the renderer does not place clone3 into the plain-ALLOW group.

verdicts.lens: SOUNDNESS/FRICTION — adversarial verification of the strict seccomp "allow-floor" proposal (does it break real containers as intended, is the profile-tracing tooling feasible, and is the inverted construction internally consistent with the renderer + CONTAINER_SECCOMP_ALLOW knob)
verdicts.evidence:
VERIFIED BY EXECUTION (x86_64 host, real installed seccomp cBPF filter; harness /tmp/floortest2.c). Under a floor = baseline ALLOW + clone arg-filter (mask 0x7e020080) + clone3->ENOSYS + defaultAction ERRNO/ENOSYS(38):
- execve -> -1/ENOSYS(38); socket(AF_INET) -> -1/ENOSYS; fork -> ENOSYS; vfork -> ENOSYS; clone3 -> ENOSYS. So exec/network/fork are broken by omission exactly as intended (SOUNDNESS claim confirmed: every real image breaks until it ships CONTAINER_SECCOMP_ALLOW).
- clone(SIGCHLD, no NEW*) -> child pid returned (works); clone(thread flags 0x10f00) -> works; clone(CLONE_NEWNS) -> ENOSYS; clone(CLONE_NEWUSER) -> ENOSYS. The arg-filter is sound: threading/fork-equiv survive, re-namespacing is blocked. Mask decode confirms 0x7e020080 covers CLONE_NEWNS|CGROUP|UTS|IPC|USER|PID|NET fully; the stray 0x80 bit is a CSIGNAL bit (no real signal=0x80), and CLONE_INTO_CGROUP is clone3-only (clone3 hard-denied), so the no-re-namespacing guarantee holds.

TOOLING FEASIBILITY VERIFIED: SCMP_ACT_LOG maps to SECCOMP_RET_LOGALLOW=0x7ffc0000 (seccomp-bpf.h:44) = kernel SECCOMP_RET_LOG (log+allow). Executed /tmp/logtest.c: under defaultAction LOG, socket() returned fd 3 (success, NOT ENOSYS) and is audit-logged. So the step-1 LOG dry-run is genuinely non-fatal and yields a complete used-set in one run. seccomp-oci.c:103 already compiles SCMP_ACT_LOG, so the 'learning profile = floor with defaultAction LOG' render is a one-flag change. strace/crun/podman/ausearch all present on host -> step-2 fallback and step-3 static seed are both feasible. Construction is internally consistent with the existing render pipeline: SECCOMP_CHUNK_NAMES=240 (seccomp-oci.c:261) comfortably holds a ~95-150 name single ALLOW group in one chunk; defaultErrnoRet=38 already in seccomp-base.json; the OCI parser (seccomp-oci.c) already handles SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ for the clone rule and per-rule errnoRet for the clone3 ENOSYS pin. The filter armed via LD_PRELOAD constructor (jail/preload.c) runs AFTER the entrypoint execve and libc init but before the workload main(), so the floor's exec-deny does NOT break container startup, only the workload's own later exec/fork — which is precisely the intended, survivable tradeoff. Net: the proposal is SOUND and the tooling makes the per-package profile discoverable in one LOG run; I recommend PASS.
issues: NOT-YET-WIRED (scope reality check, not a defect of the design): seccomp-render.uc is invoked nowhere in the build, oci-policy.uc never sets cfg.linux.seccomp, and container.mk emits seccomp_allow=... into policy.kv but oci-policy.uc never reads it. So the 'invert the model' work is greenfield wiring on top of an UNUSED renderer — the current renderer is only a deny-delta (base MINUS tighten.list) and the CONTAINER_SECCOMP_ALLOW knob is presently dead. The UNION words(CONTAINER_SECCOMP_ALLOW) half of floor_allow() does not exist yet and must be added to BOTH the renderer and oci-policy.uc/jail wiring.

PROVENANCE ERROR in the task framing: seccomp-analysis.json is cited as a prototype of the strict floor, but it is the OLD runtime-consensus model. Its 47 'allow' decisions EXPLICITLY allow execve, execveat, socket, clone3, memfd_create, setuid, setsockopt, seccomp, mknod, splice, io_setup — every one of which the new proposal moves to OPTIN or HARDDENY. The analysis.json corpus therefore CANNOT be used as the static seed (step 3) without first inverting/filtering its decisions; feeding its consensus 'allows' in would silently re-grant exec+network and defeat the floor.

OPENAT AMBIGUITY (potential FALSE-DENY that would brick everything incl. the LOG bootstrap): the classification text lists openat2/creat as OPTIN and describes baseline as 'existing-fd I/O' without clearly stating plain open/openat is in baseline. Executed under a baseline that omitted openat: openat(read) -> ENOSYS. If the real baseline drops openat, NO container can open its own config/cert/dev-node at runtime, breaking even traefik-whoami's TLS path AND making the LOG-profiling run useless (the app dies on first config read instead of logging a clean superset). The baseline MUST include read-path openat (and almost certainly newfstatat/getdents64) or the whole scheme collapses. RECOMMEND: pin open/openat/newfstatat/getdents64/lseek into baseline_allow explicitly and state it.

GLIBC-INIT FALSE-DENY observed empirically: my first harness aborted with 'malloc(): corrupted top size' AFTER install because glibc stdio/malloc hit a syscall not in my representative baseline (likely brk-growth/newfstatat during printf). The preload arms after libc init so this is normally fine, but it demonstrates the baseline must cover the libc allocator/stdio fast path (brk, mmap, mremap, newfstatat). Any baseline that is even slightly too tight will SIGABRT the workload on first malloc/printf, not return a clean ENOSYS — the failure mode is a crash, not a graceful fallback. The LOG-render must therefore use the SAME name-set as the ERRNO floor (proposal says it does) so the learning run exercises the identical allow set.

SOCKET ARG-FILTER PROSE IS WRONG and would mislead an implementer: proposal says 'the no-CAP_AUDIT_WRITE branch is the only reachable one -- we keep exactly that branch.' Inspection of seccomp-base.json shows socket has FOUR groups with excludes.caps=[CAP_AUDIT_WRITE] (1 ERRNO for the netlink-audit socket domain=16/proto=9, plus 3 SCMP_CMP_NE ALLOW groups that together open AF_INET) and one 5th group with includes.caps=[CAP_AUDIT_WRITE] that the renderer drops. So opting socket in must copy 4 groups (the unconditional NE-allow is what actually permits AF_INET), not 1. Also the renderer skips on includes.caps, never excludes.caps — the proposal conflates the two. Net behavior is achievable but the description is incorrect.

COUNT INCONSISTENCY in the spec: the task simultaneously states baseline is '96 syscalls (95 unconditional + clone)', 'the hardcoded ~150-name list', and '~150 names'. 96 vs 150 is a ~1.5x discrepancy that must be resolved before anyone hardcodes the list; given the openat/libc-init names that MUST be added (prior issue), the real number is likely closer to the 96-110 range only if file-open is excluded, which is itself the dangerous case. The 'roughly 3x reduction' claim depends on which count is real.

ARCH-ORACLE FRAGILITY (acknowledged but worth flagging): using moby seccomp-base.json as the arch_available oracle means any baseline name the base never mentions is kept unconditionally on ALL arches (futex_waitv, epoll_pwait2, clock_*_time64, rseq, etc.). On arches lacking those the kernel returns ENOSYS for the syscall NUMBER anyway, so a stray ALLOW entry is harmless — BUT find_syscall() in seccomp-oci.c silently drops names unknown to procd's syscall-names table (seccomp-oci.c:360-365), so a baseline name that procd's table lacks on a given arch is dropped from the filter with only a DEBUG log, not an error. A typo or arch-missing core name fails open (name absent from ALLOW group => hits defaultAction ENOSYS) rather than loud — acceptable for safety but invisible; recommend the render emit a build-time warning when a baseline name is absent from the target syscall table.
